summary: Spain is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-exempt list can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: the Schengen Borders Code counts the 180-day period preceding each day of stay, so days already spent anywhere in the area during that period still count against the 90. The Schengen Borders Code counts the date of entry as the first day of stay and the date of exit as the last.

source.name: Schengen Borders Code (Regulation (EU) 2016/399), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/399 (Schengen Borders Code), Article 6(1) — no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, considering the 180-day period preceding each day of stay; Article 6(2) — date of entry is the first day of stay, date of exit the last

fee.notes: Children 6–11: €45; under 6: free. The fee is set EU-wide by the Visa Code; Spain's Order AUC/891/2024 says the €90 fee has applied since 11 June 2024.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 establishing a Community Code on Visas, Article 16(1) (visa fee), Article 1(1) (stays not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period) and Article 24(1) (a visa may be issued for one, two or multiple entries; validity up to five years, set on examination of each application), consolidated to 11 June 2024

applyWindow.text: The EU Visa Code says an application is lodged no more than six months before the start of the visit and, as a rule, no later than 15 calendar days before it; in justified urgent cases the consulate may accept it later.

source.name: EU Visa Code — Regulation (EC) No 810/2009, Article 9(1) (consolidated text)

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and/or photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders, and passports are no longer stamped. Registration happens at the border on your first crossing since the EES started; the EU says it can be quicker if you register some data in advance at a self-service kiosk or through a mobile app, where available.

source.name: EES — Official EU website

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.

source.name: European Union — ETIAS: frequently asked questions

notes: Under EU rules, travellers arriving from outside the EU may bring in 200 cigarettes, 1 litre of spirits and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 when arriving by air or sea) duty-free.
Between EU countries, no further duty or tax is due on alcohol and tobacco bought for your own use, though customs may check that the quantities are for personal use.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says to be alert to street crime: thieves use distraction techniques and often work in teams, so take care of passports, money and belongings, particularly when checking in or collecting luggage at the airport and while arranging car hire.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Spain — days spent in France or Italy count against the same allowance.

The UK Foreign Office says that under the EU's Entry/Exit System you may be asked to give biometric details every time you enter or exit the Schengen area, and that the checks can take extra time, so allow more time at the border.
ETIAS is not in operation yet, and no applications are being collected. The EU's official ETIAS website is travel-europe.europa.eu.
Canada's travel advice says pickpocketing and bag snatching are common, especially in Madrid and Barcelona, and that thieves often target tourists at weekends, holidays and festivals.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Spain?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Spain and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Spain Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Spain?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once it starts, the online authorization costs €20 (under-18s and over-70s are exempt from the fee) and is valid for three years or until your passport expires.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Spain?
faq.answer: It is mandatory for Schengen visa applicants: medical coverage of at least €30,000 valid throughout the Schengen Area.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Spain without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area — time in Spain and other Schengen countries shares the same allowance.
